newsitem.title: FRANCE: BA French unit forecasts profit in two years.
newsitem.headline: BA French unit forecasts profit in two years.

text.p: French airline Air Liberte-TAT will not break even this year but expects to turn profitable in two years, chairman Marc Rochet said on Saturday.

"This year, we will not quite break even but we should get there in two years," he told Radio Classique. "Our objective is have revenue of more than three billion francs and profitability in two years".
Air Liberte-TAT is the French subsidiary of British Airways Plc . The private French Rivaud group also holds a small stake.

Traffic for the summer appeared to confirm the trend seen in the first half, which saw growth of five or six percent on its domestic and regional routes and long-haul routes to French overseas departments, Rochet said.
He said Air Liberte-TAT was not interested in buying rival airline AOM, owned by the state-backed Consortium de Realisations (CDR) holding company.

"AOM today does not interest us in the short term. Simply because we have an enormous task on our hands with merging and bringing TAT and Air Liberte under a single banner," Rochet said, adding that there was also a lack of clarity over CDR's intentions for AOM.

However, he said, "we are watching them for two reasons: firstly, because it is an airline in competition with Air Liberte...the second reason is that AOM is today a subsidiary of CDR whose mission is not clear to everyone".
